title: Quantization rollout monitoring + alerting requirements (SRE)
content:
Owner: Aisha (SLO dashboards)
Last updated: 2025-02-07
Audience: SRE oncall + runtime/platform owners + product (Optimize)
Scope: dashboards + alerts for the opt-in Quantization Profile Library rollout (Hosted first, then Dedicated/Private parity).

---

1) Purpose / what “good” looks like

We need a standard set of dashboards + alerting rules so we can safely enable route-scoped quantization profiles (int8/int4 etc) while maintaining reliability + latency SLOs and quickly identifying regressions.

A successful rollout monitoring package should:
- Make it obvious which traffic is quantized vs baseline, and which profile/version is active.
- Allow fast segmentation by: route, customer/org, model, profile version, GPU SKU, region, kernel path.
- Detect: (a) reliability regressions, (b) performance regressions, (c) profile resolution/compat issues, (d) cache/registry issues, (e) cost attribution gaps.
- Provide direct links to rollback steps and “disable quantization for this route/customer” actions.

Non-goals:
- Deep model-quality evaluation dashboards (those live in eval harness tooling). We only need “quality regression signal present” + correlation markers here.

---

2) Required dimensions (tags) for all quantization-related time series

These must exist as tags/labels on metrics emitted by serving + routing + gateway. If any are missing, dashboards will be low value.

Minimum required dimensions:
- env (prod/staging)
- region (us-east-1, eu-west-1, etc)
- deployment_mode (hosted | dedicated | private)
- org_id
- customer_id (optional if multi-tenant orgs; if unavailable, still require org_id)
- route_id (the unit for enablement)
- route_name (human readable)
- model_id (catalog identifier)
- model_version (serving version)
- execution_mode (baseline | quantized)
- quant_profile_id
- quant_profile_version
- quant_dtype (fp16/bf16/int8/int4)
- kernel_path (baseline_kernels | quant_kernels | fallback_baseline | unknown)
- gpu_sku (e.g., A100-80GB, H100, L4)
- gpu_arch (sm80/sm90)

Strongly recommended additional dimensions:
- request_type (chat | completion | embeddings | rerank)
- context_length_bin (0-1k, 1k-4k, 4k-16k, 16k+)
- output_length_bin
- batching_enabled (true/false)
- cache_hit (prefix/KV cache; true/false/unknown)

Notes:
- We need to be careful about cardinality. org_id+route_id is already high. At minimum, dashboards must support aggregated views (top N routes by volume) and selective filtering for investigations.

---

3) Dashboard package (minimum viable set)

3.1 Executive/rollout overview: “Quantization rollout health (prod)”

Primary questions this answers:
- How much traffic is quantized right now (overall + by region + by model)?
- Are we seeing any reliability/latency regressions correlated with quantization?
- Are fallbacks happening (and why)?

Panels (time series + single stat):
A) Quantized traffic share
- % requests with execution_mode=quantized / total
- Breakdowns: by region, by model_id

B) Error rate comparison
- 5xx rate (quantized vs baseline) overlaid
- 4xx rate (esp. 429) to catch rate-limit side effects

C) Latency comparison
- p50, p95 end-to-end request latency (quantized vs baseline)
- p95 “time to first token” for streaming routes

D) Throughput + saturation indicators
- tokens/sec (aggregate)
- GPU utilization (if available), queue time, scheduler wait

E) Fallback indicators
- fallback_rate = requests where execution_mode requested quantized but kernel_path=fallback_baseline
- top fallback reasons (see 3.4)

F) Profile resolution + registry health
- profile_fetch_errors
- profile_signature_verification_failures
- cache_refresh_latency

G) Canary state snapshot
- top N routes with canary enabled + their canary percent
- number of auto-disables in last 24h (by reason)

Navigation links:
- Link to “Per-route deep dive” dashboard with a pre-populated filter for route_id.
- Link to rollback runbook.


3.2 Per-route deep dive: “Route quantization health”

Entry points:
- Oncall investigation
- Support escalations (“my JSON mode broke when quantization enabled”) usually route-scoped

Must-have filters:
- org_id (optional)
- route_id (required)
- model_id
- quant_profile_id + version
- gpu_sku + region

Panels:
A) Route request volume
- req/s total, split by execution_mode

B) Route latency
- p50/p95 e2e
- TTFT p50/p95 (if streaming)
- server compute time vs queue time breakdown (if available)

C) Route reliability
- 5xx rate, 5xx count
- top error codes/messages (log-derived if metrics unavailable)
- timeout rate

D) Output/token metrics (to detect subtle regressions)
- output_tokens p50/p95
- input_tokens p50/p95
- aborted/interrupt rate

E) Quantization-specifics
- fallback_rate and reasons
- quant_profile_version currently resolved (and changes over time)
- incompatibility checks triggered (gpu arch mismatch, unsupported kernel, seq length regime unsupported)

F) Audit/controls surface
- most recent route quantization setting changes (from audit log stream)
- current route setting: enabled/disabled + canary percent + allowlist/denylist overrides (if applicable)


3.3 Per-profile/version view: “Profile rollout + safety”

Purpose: ensure a profile version isn’t causing broad regressions across multiple routes.

Filters:
- model_id
- quant_profile_id
- quant_profile_version

Panels:
- Active routes count (how many routes are using this profile)
- Request volume and traffic share
- p95 latency delta vs baseline (aggregate)
- 5xx delta vs baseline (aggregate)
- Fallback rate (aggregate)
- Incompatibility reasons histogram
- Regions/GPU SKUs where the profile is active


3.4 Runtime/infra view: “Quantization plumbing health (serving/runtime)”

Purpose: catch failures caused by cache stampedes, registry latency, signature verification issues, etc.

Panels:
- profile artifact fetch latency p50/p95
- fetch error rate by status code
- cache hit rate for profile lookups
- cache refresh/invalidation events rate
- worker restart rate correlated with profile refresh
- signature verification failures (should be ~0; page on any sustained non-zero)
- “unknown kernel_path” or missing tags % (observability regressions)


3.5 Dedicated/Private parity view (phase 2)

For Dedicated/Private deployments we need the same dashboards but allow filtering by tenant cluster / deployment id (to be defined).

---

4) Alerting requirements (suggested thresholds)

Guiding principle: we want a fast signal during canaries without paging the world for normal variance. Prefer multi-window + burn-rate style for SLOs, but we also need quantization-specific guardrails that trigger auto-disable.

Definitions used below:
- “baseline” = same route/model traffic where execution_mode=baseline (or “quantization disabled”).
- “quantized” = execution_mode=quantized.
- “delta” = quantized - baseline (absolute or relative depending on metric).

4.1 Page alerts (human must respond)

A) Quantization-correlated 5xx spike (route-scoped)
- Condition (5m window):
  - quantized 5xx_rate >= 0.5% AND
  - delta vs baseline >= +0.3% absolute AND
  - quantized requests >= 300 in window
- Action:
  - Auto-disable quantization for the route (if canary/auto-disable enabled) + page oncall.

B) Broad 5xx spike correlated with a profile version (profile-scoped)
- Condition (10m window):
  - For a given quant_profile_id+version: 5xx_rate >= 0.3% AND
  - total requests for that profile >= 5k AND
  - 5xx_rate is >= 2x baseline aggregate for same model_id
- Action:
  - Freeze further rollouts of that profile version (release engineering hook) + page runtime/platform oncall.

C) Profile resolution failures (platform plumbing)
- profile_fetch_error_rate >= 1% for 10m OR signature verification failures > 0 sustained for 2m
- Action:
  - Page runtime/platform oncall; likely need to fail closed to baseline and investigate registry/network.

D) Latency regression severe (route-scoped)
- Condition (10m window):
  - p95 latency quantized >= 1.25x baseline AND
  - delta >= +150ms AND
  - quantized requests >= 500
- Action:
  - Auto-disable route + page oncall (if user-facing). For background/batch routes, may be ticket-level depending on severity.

E) Cache stampede / refresh storm recurrence
- Condition:
  - profile cache refresh events rate spikes >= 10x normal AND
  - concurrent fetches per worker exceed configured limit (needs metric)
- Action:
  - Page oncall (risk of cascading failures).


4.2 Ticket alerts (notify + investigate during biz hours unless customer impact)

A) Elevated fallback_rate
- fallback_rate >= 5% for 30m for any route with quantization enabled
- Investigation:
  - likely mis-scoped profile for gpu_sku/arch or seq length bins; audit recent profile publish or route config.

B) Mild latency regression
- p95 latency quantized >= 1.10x baseline for 30m

C) Increased timeout rate
- request timeouts +0.1% absolute vs baseline for 30m

D) Missing tagging / observability regression
- % of requests missing quant_profile_id/version tags >= 0.5% for 30m
- Goal is to prevent “unknown unknowns” where quantized traffic is unaccounted.


4.3 Auto-disable triggers (no page by default, but log + annotate)

These are intended to be safe, fast rollback levers and should write an audit event with reason.

A) Quality regression signal (external)
- If quality regression signal is emitted for org_id+route_id+profile_id (from eval/monitoring), then:
  - Set route quantization enabled=false OR canary_percent=0
  - Emit annotation “auto-disabled: quality_regression_signal”
- Page only if:
  - impacted route is tagged interactive=true OR has high volume threshold.

B) Incompatibility mismatch (sustained)
- If incompatibility/fallback due to gpu mismatch > 20% for 10m, auto-disable (avoid thrash).

---

5) Segmentation + investigation workflow (required UX in dashboards)

When debugging a customer complaint, the workflow should be:
1) Filter by org_id and route_id.
2) Confirm if quantization is enabled and what the canary percent is.
3) Confirm execution_mode split (is traffic actually quantized?).
4) Identify resolved quant_profile_id/version and kernel_path.
5) Compare key metrics baseline vs quantized:
   - p95 latency, TTFT
   - 5xx rate and top errors
   - output token distribution (format changes sometimes correlate with truncation/length)
6) If regression present: one-click link to rollback runbook and/or to the route settings page.
7) After disable: verify recovery within 5–10 minutes.

Dashboards must include:
- A “baseline vs quantized” toggle overlay (same chart, two lines).
- Annotations on charts when:
  - route config changed (enable/disable/canary percent)
  - profile version changed
  - auto-disable triggered

---

6) Data sources + instrumentation requirements (implementation notes)

Metrics/tracing
- Quantization tags are expected to be available per PR: add_quantization_execution_metrics_tags.
- We need consistent naming for:
  - execution_mode
  - quant_profile_id/version
  - kernel_path
  - fallback_reason

Logging
- Errors must include structured fields: route_id, org_id, model_id, quant_profile_id/version, gpu_sku, kernel_path, fallback_reason.

Audit logs
- Route settings updates (Console/API) should emit audit events that can be surfaced as dashboard annotations.
- Auto-disable must also emit an audit event with:
  - reason
  - triggering metric snapshot (string summary acceptable)

Cost attribution
- Cost metrics should be segmented by execution_mode + profile_id/version so we can validate the business goal (tokens/$) without guessing.
- SRE requirement: if cost attribution tags are missing, create a ticket alert (see 4.2D).

---

7) Suggested initial dashboard filters (reduce cardinality pain)

Default dashboard views should show:
- Top 20 routes by request volume in last 1h (with ability to search route_id)
- Top 10 orgs by quantized traffic volume (optional; gated by permissions)
- Top 10 profiles by traffic

For per-route dashboard default time range: last 6 hours.
For rollout overview default time range: last 24 hours.

---

8) Open questions / follow-ups

1) What is the authoritative list of fallback reasons and their mapping to runtime/platform components?
   - Proposed: gpu_arch_mismatch, kernel_unsupported, seq_len_out_of_range, profile_fetch_failed, signature_invalid, runtime_exception, unknown.

2) Do we have a stable “interactive route” tag to differentiate paging severity?

3) For Private deployments: do we have access to the same metric tags, or do we need a reduced set?

4) Where will the dashboard live (Grafana org structure) and what is the RBAC story for org_id/customer_id filtering?

---

9) Action items (as of 2025-02-07)

- (Logan / Nadia) Confirm metric tag taxonomy + ensure cost attribution has execution_mode + profile_id/version.
- (Rafael / Sean) Define which alerts should trigger auto-disable vs page.
- (Felix) Confirm dashboard UX for baseline vs quantized overlays + annotations.
- (Mateo / Hiro) Provide canonical fallback_reason enumeration + ensure emitted consistently.
- (Jordan) Confirm route_id naming/identity stability across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.

End.
